To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal adaptation strategy depends on the rate of change and the rate of change is a function of both the physical and social systems.

(1) the rate of change in climate is an important consideration when developing adaptation strategies; (2) the optimal adaptation strategy depends on a number of factors, including rates of sea-level change, discount rates, and depreciation rates; and (3) adaptation to some amount of sea-level change may not be the best strategy for coastal development.
the determination of the optimal adaptation strategy depends on taking into accounts the future rates of climate change as well as social constraints and political considerations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to adapt to climate change in a world in which climate continues to change.
the development and application of a quantitative framework that can be used to assess adaptation to sea-level change and to other types of climate change.
the optimal timing of adaptation strategies, which is a key question in climate adaptation research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of sea-level change is important for determining the timing, scale, and cost of coastal adaptation.
adaptation to sea-level change is a complex issue that requires consideration of the rate of change as well as the amount of sea-level change.
adaptation is a process of adjustment that is designed to moderate the adverse effects of climate change, and to exploit the beneficial opportunities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adaptation strategies that do not take into account rates of climate change may result in sub-optimal outcomes.
we should not only adapt to the amount of climate change, but also to its rates of change.
adaptation strategies need to consider rates of change, and that adaptation to rates of change can produce better outcomes than adaptation to a fixed amount of climate change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of change of a climate variable is an important factor that should be incorporated when developing adaptation strategies.
adaptation decisions should be informed by a consideration of the rate and magnitude of future change.
adaptation to rates of change may be more effective than adaptation to amounts of change, and that adaptation decisions should take rates of change into account.
